gloss: once only; one-off; just one time

definitions.gloss: once only; just one time; one-off
definitions.explanation: Something that happens only once and will not be repeated. Emphasizes the singularity and finality of the occurrence.

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}は{一回|いっかい}きりだ。
その{店|みせ}には{一回|いっかい}きりしか{行|い}ったことがない。
examples.english: I've only been to that store once.

examples.japanese: {一回|いっかい}きりのチャンスを{逃|のが}すわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I can't afford to miss this one-time chance.

notes:
{一回|いっかい}きり emphasizes that something happens only once and will not be repeated. It conveys finality and often a sense of preciousness.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- As adverb: {一回|いっかい}きりしか{行|い}ったことがない (I've only been once)
- As noun modifier: {一回|いっかい}きりの{出会|であ}い (a once-in-a-lifetime encounter)
- As predicate: {人生|じんせい}は{一回|いっかい}きりだ (you only live once)

THE SUFFIX きり:
きり means 'only' or 'limited to,' emphasizing a boundary. It attaches to quantities: {一人|ひとり}きり (all alone), {一度|いちど}きり (only once).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一度|いちど}きり: only once (same meaning, slightly more formal)
- たった{一回|いっかい}: just one time (emphasizes smallness of the number)
- {一回|いっかい}だけ: only once (neutral, less emphatic)
